title: Affine coherent edge isomorphisms compatible with base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $K=Rf_*(G[0])$ in $D(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $A=H^0(K)$, $E=H^1(K)$. Assume $A,E$ are finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], $K$ is Zariski-locally isomorphic to $A[0]\oplus E[-1]$, and for every scheme morphism $g:T\to S$ the canonical module base-change map $\delta_g:Lg^*K\to Rf_{T,*}(G_T[0])$ [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map] is an isomorphism. Here $X_T=X\times_ST$, $f_T:X_T\to T$, $j_T:X_T\to X$, $G_T=j_T^*G$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback]; $E[-1]$ places $E$ in cohomological degree one. Let $\tau:K\to E[-1]$ be the canonical truncation morphism inducing the identity on $H^1$. The map $\gamma_g=H^1(Lg^*\tau):H^1(Lg^*K)\to g^*E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is invertible. Write $\beta_g=H^1(\delta_g)\gamma_g^{-1}:g^*E\to R^1f_{T,*}G_T$. For every affine $T$ and $g:T\to S$, the canonical Leray edge $\varepsilon_T:H^1(X_T,G_T)\to\Gamma(T,R^1f_{T,*}G_T)$ [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections, pqf-def-cohomology] is invertible, and
$$e_g=\Gamma(T,\beta_g^{-1})\varepsilon_T:H^1(X_T,G_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,g^*E)$$
is $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-linear. These maps are simultaneous and compatible with every $S$-morphism $h:T'\to T$ between affine base schemes:
$$e_{gh}\circ h_X^*=\rho_h\circ e_g.$$
Here $h_X:X_{T'}\to X_T$, its coefficient morphism is the canonical $h_X^*G_T\cong G_{T'}$, and $h_X^*$ is the resulting module cohomology map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]; $\rho_h$ is section pullback followed by $h^*g^*E\cong(gh)^*E$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 0ATM, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 01FB, remark-explain-arrow; Tag 01F8, lemma-functoriality; Tag 01F2, lemma-Leray. Application of these constructions to a two-degree locally free derived direct image.

proof.text: The given local splitting shows K is in D≤1: above degree one the homology of both single summands vanishes. Exact open restriction commutes with homology, and a module sheaf zero on a covering is zero. The canonical projection τ is constructed by the bijection from maps K→H1(K)[-1] to maps on H1, so it induces the identity.

Apply the specified top-cohomology pullback theorem in degree one. Its κ is definitionally gamma for τ. The theorem makes gamma invertible; the base-change hypothesis makes H1(delta) invertible. Define beta as inverse gamma followed by H1(delta). The normalization equation follows by cancellation.

For every affine base T, the base-changed map is qcqs and the tensor-pulled coefficient is quasi-coherent, via the unique adjunction-preserving tensor-to-ordinary pullback isomorphism. Affine higher-direct-image cohomology vanishing and the canonical Leray degeneration theorem make epsilon invertible. Naturality of epsilon at multiplication, the scalar-action formula for module cohomology and functoriality of higher direct image make epsilon linear after restricting scalars along f_T. Compose with sections of beta inverse to construct e.

For h:T′→T, form the canonical base-change map m for f_T,h and h_X, followed by Rf_(gh),* of the specified coefficient isomorphism. Apply normalized tensor single-module horizontal pasting to obtain Lh*(delta_g) followed by m equals derived composition followed by delta_gh.

The top pullback theorem gives the upper bound for Lg*K, transported across delta_g to K_g. Naturality of κ at delta_g and the composition identity for κ imply h*(beta_g) followed by b_h equals ordinary composition followed by beta_gh, where b_h is inverse κ_(h,K_g) followed by H1(m). Precompose by the invertible κ_(h,Lg*K) followed by h*(κ_g), apply those equations and pasting, then cancel. A generic categorical calculation carries out this cancellation without unfolding the sheaf functors.

Apply the top-degree Leray commutative-square identity to f_T,f_(gh),h,h_X and the explicit canonical coefficient isomorphism. This gives epsilon_(gh) after the specified cohomology pullback equals sections of b_h after section pullback and epsilon_g.

Postcompose the preceding equation with sections of beta_gh inverse. The beta composition identity replaces b_h followed by beta_gh inverse with h*(beta_g inverse) followed by ordinary composition. Naturality of the normalized tensor adjunction unit moves beta_g inverse across section pullback. The resulting expression is exactly rho_h after e_g.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0ATM, 01FB, 01E4 and 01F4(2), with top-cohomology comparison. Local splitting is used only for the upper bound; qcqs higher-direct-image vanishing replaces the local K-flat calculation.
